entries.definition: Authorization model that decides on properties of the user, resource and context; in ISC, rules keyed on identity attributes such as department or location drive role membership criteria and dynamic assignment.

Microsoft's on-premises Windows directory of users, groups and organizational units; ISC reaches it through a virtual appliance and the IQService to aggregate accounts and groups and to create, modify and disable accounts.

Symmetric block cipher, typically used with 256-bit keys, that protects tenant data and stored credentials at rest; being symmetric distinguishes it from the public and private key pairs used to protect source credentials on appliances.
Prebuilt server image for launching an instance in Amazon's cloud; SailPoint shares one so engineers can run a virtual appliance as an EC2 instance instead of on VMware or Hyper-V.

Programmatic contract that lets scripts and external systems read and change tenant objects; ISC exposes versioned endpoints for identities, sources, roles, workflows and more so admins can automate work done by hand in the console.
Public cloud provider on which the ISC multi-tenant platform runs; it is also a common governed source, where a connector manages cloud accounts, groups and permission sets.

Service on each virtual appliance that hosts connectors and relays aggregation and provisioning traffic between on-premises sources and the tenant; its log file is the first place to look when connector operations fail.

Notation such as 10.0.0.0/16 that describes an address range by prefix length; engineers use it when planning appliance subnets and firewall rules and to avoid ranges that clash with the appliance's internal container networks.
Text tool driven by typed commands; SailPoint's open-source one lets engineers call APIs, test transforms, run searches, and manage workflows and connectors from a terminal or a pipeline.
Processor resource of a server; appliance sizing specifies a minimum number of virtual cores, and sustained high usage in health checks points to an undersized appliance or heavy aggregation load.
Plain-text table format with one record per line; ISC uses it for delimited file sources, bulk uploads of accounts, entitlements or roles, and exports of search results and reports.

Full directory path that uniquely locates an object, such as CN=Ann,OU=Sales,DC=corp; ISC uses it as the account ID on directory sources and builds it with a provisioning policy or transform for new accounts.
Service that turns host names into addresses; an appliance depends on it to reach the tenant and source servers, so wrong resolver settings are a frequent cause of failed connectivity tests.

Plans and redundancy that restore service after a major outage; for ISC this means placing appliances of a cluster in more than one site so source connectivity survives losing a data center, while SailPoint covers the cloud side.

Business suite such as SAP or Oracle that runs finance, purchasing and payroll; its roles and transaction codes are high-risk entitlements and frequent subjects of conflict policies and focused reviews.
European Union privacy law governing personal data; ISC supports it through least-privilege access, periodic reviews, audit trails and prompt removal of access when people leave.
128-bit value generated so that it never repeats; Active Directory's objectGUID serves as a stable native key for accounts across renames, and ISC object IDs are similar 32-character hex strings.
Design goal of keeping a service running through component failure; an engineer deploys at least two virtual appliances in each cluster so one keeps processing if the other goes down.

entries.expansion: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act
entries.definition: US law protecting patient health information; healthcare tenants use access reviews, conflict policies and audit reports in ISC to show who can reach clinical systems and why.
Business function that hires, moves and terminates workers; its system of record is usually the authoritative source that creates identities and drives joiner, mover and leaver events in ISC.
Application such as Workday or SAP SuccessFactors that holds employee records; ISC typically connects it as the authoritative source whose attributes feed identity profiles and lifecycle states.

Encrypted web protocol on port 443 that carries console sessions, API calls and appliance-to-tenant traffic; appliances need only outbound connections of this kind, so no inbound firewall ports are opened.

Overall discipline and tooling for creating digital identities, authenticating them and controlling what they can reach; governance platforms like ISC sit on top of it to add oversight, reviews and compliance evidence.
Former name of SailPoint's cloud governance platform before its rebranding; it still appears in older documentation, API and tenant host names, and rule and connector names.
Service that authenticates users and issues assertions to applications; ISC can trust an external one, such as Okta or Entra ID, for sign-in to the tenant, or play that role for other apps.

Discipline of controlling who has access to what, proving it is appropriate and removing it when no longer needed, through lifecycle automation, requests, reviews and policies; it is the core purpose of ISC.

SailPoint's self-hosted governance product; it differs from ISC in that customers run its servers and database, and its free-form BeanShell rules contrast with ISC's restricted, SailPoint-reviewed rules.
Addressing scheme for hosts on a network; appliances need a static or reserved address, and some sources and firewalls allow-list the addresses that appliance or tenant traffic comes from.
SailPoint's multi-tenant SaaS platform for identity governance, covering sources, identity profiles, roles, access requests, certifications, workflows and APIs, administered from a browser console.
Practice and tools, such as ServiceNow, for handling tickets and service requests; ISC integrates with them so changes on sources lacking a direct connector become tickets fulfilled by a person.
Java standard for reaching relational databases through a driver; ISC's generic database connector uses it, with a connection URL, a driver JAR uploaded to the source and SQL queries for aggregation.

Shorthand for the three identity lifecycle events of someone starting, changing role or department, and departing; ISC automates each with lifecycle states, role assignment and event-triggered workflows.
Text format of key-value objects and arrays used in every ISC API request and response, and to define transforms, workflows, source configurations and exported tenant configuration.
Signed, base64-encoded credential carrying claims about the caller; ISC's OAuth endpoint returns one as the bearer access token that scripts send on every API call until it expires.

Identity attribute, stored as cloudLifecycleState, that says where a person is in employment, such as active or inactive; each value on an identity profile can enable or disable accounts and grant or remove access profiles.
Standard protocol for querying and updating directory servers on port 389, or 636 when encrypted; generic directory connectors in ISC use it to aggregate and provision accounts and groups.

Requiring two or more kinds of proof, such as a password plus a phone prompt, at sign-in; ISC admins choose these methods per identity profile, and they are commonly demanded before sensitive admin actions.

entries.expansion: National Institute of Standards and Technology
entries.definition: US agency whose frameworks, such as the SP 800-53 control catalog, many organizations map to; governance programs cite it when designing reviews, least privilege and account management.
Protocol that keeps server clocks synchronized; an appliance whose clock drifts can fail authentication and certificate checks with the tenant, so time sync is part of appliance troubleshooting.

Container inside a directory domain that groups users, groups or computers for delegation and policy; directory sources in ISC are often scoped to chosen ones and move new or disabled accounts into a specific one.

Single-file package of a preconfigured virtual machine; SailPoint distributes its appliance image this way for VMware, so engineers import it into vSphere rather than building the operating system themselves.
Tools that vault, broker and record use of high-risk admin accounts; ISC complements them by governing who may hold privileged entitlements and flagging those entitlements for tighter review.
Client ID and secret pair that a user generates under their own identity in ISC; scripts exchange it for an API bearer token, and it acts with that user's level and chosen scopes.

entries.expansion: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard
entries.definition: Rules set by the major card brands requiring restricted, reviewed and logged access to cardholder environments; ISC certifications and access history provide evidence for its access-control requirements.

Data that can single out a person, such as name, home address or national ID; engineers limit which such attributes are aggregated into the tenant and keep them out of searches and exports where possible.

System of certificate authorities, certificates and key pairs that establishes trust; it underpins encrypted links to sources and the tenant, and appliances may need an internal root certificate added to trust local servers.
Granting access by job function rather than one person at a time; in ISC, roles bundle access profiles and can be assigned automatically by membership criteria on identity attributes.
Architectural style for web APIs that applies HTTP verbs such as GET, POST, PATCH and DELETE to resource URLs; all ISC public APIs follow it and exchange JSON bodies.

Delivery model where the vendor hosts, patches and scales an application used through a browser; ISC is delivered this way, unlike self-hosted IdentityIQ, and many governed sources are such applications too.
XML-based federation standard in which an identity provider sends a signed assertion to a service provider; ISC uses it for single sign-on into the tenant and can sit on either side of the exchange.
REST and JSON standard for creating, updating and removing users and groups across systems; ISC offers a connector for SaaS applications that expose such an endpoint, avoiding a custom integration.
ISC component that turns provisioning for sources without direct connectors into tickets in a help-desk platform such as ServiceNow, then polls ticket status to confirm the change was made.
Libraries and tools for building against a platform; SailPoint publishes them for languages such as TypeScript, Python, Go and PowerShell, plus one for writing custom SaaS connectors.
Platform that collects and correlates logs for threat detection and audit; ISC audit events can be forwarded to one such as Splunk so security teams can watch identity activity alongside other logs.
Contract terms for availability, response and support; also used internally for how quickly approvals or tickets must close, which ISC reminders and escalations help meet.
Protocol servers use to send email; ISC notifications for approvals, reminders and certifications travel over it, and engineers verify sender domains and templates when configuring tenant email.
Principle that one person should not hold conflicting access, such as creating and approving payments; ISC policies of this type flag violating combinations during requests and certifications.
US law requiring public companies to prove controls over financial reporting; it is a major driver of periodic access certifications and conflict policies for finance applications governed in ISC.

In federation, the application that relies on an external authority's assertion instead of checking passwords itself; ISC plays this role when an organization's own login service handles tenant sign-in.
Language for reading and changing relational databases; JDBC sources in ISC run SELECT statements to aggregate accounts and groups and can run statements or stored procedures to provision.
Encrypted remote login protocol; engineers connect to a virtual appliance this way as the sailpoint user to run diagnostic commands, read logs and test connectivity to sources and the tenant.
Authenticating once to reach many applications without new prompts; ISC can provide it to apps or accept it from an external identity provider for access to the tenant console.
Protocol that encrypts data in transit using certificates; it protects connections from appliances to the tenant and, when enabled, from connectors to sources such as directories on port 636.
The browser console where admins and users work; tasks done there, such as editing sources or reviewing access, can also be scripted through the APIs the console itself calls.
Sign-in name of the form ann@corp.com on an Active Directory account; it is a common correlation attribute and is often built by a transform when provisioning new accounts.

Web address such as https://acme.identitynow.com; engineers must know the tenant's console address and its separate API gateway address, and appliances must reach a published list of them through the firewall.
SailPoint-supplied virtual machine in the customer network that hosts connectors and securely relays traffic between on-premises sources and the tenant, opening every connection outbound.
Software-defined computer running on a hypervisor such as VMware ESXi, Hyper-V or a cloud instance; each SailPoint appliance is deployed as one with set processor, memory and disk minimums.
Isolated network inside a public cloud account; engineers deploying appliances in the cloud place them in one with outbound routes to the tenant and private routes to the sources.
Tagged text format used in SAML metadata and assertions and by some older web-service connectors; admins exchange such files between parties when setting up federated sign-in.
